title: The world's leading AI companies are all struggling to contain their latest models
excerpt: There's been a recent string of cybersecurity incidents among the world's leading AI models. Here's a look at what's happened.
content_html:
By Lakshmi Varanasi

You're currently following this author! Want to unfollow? Unsubscribe via the link in your email.

The most powerful AI models keep going awry, according to the companies building them.

The disclosures come as frontier AI models get more powerful and more capable of acting autonomously. They also highlight a growing challenge for the companies building them —the systems designed to test increasingly capable models can have weaknesses of their own.

Over the past few weeks, multiple frontier AI models have accessed real systems during cybersecurity testing.

Researchers on Friday said China's popular new Kimi K3 model, made by Moonshot AI, circumvented restrictions in its test environment. Anthropic and Meta also said recently that their own latest models have done things they aren't supposed to. OpenAI kicked it all off last month when its models went to great — and worrisome — lengths to hack into another company.

Amid heightened concern, OpenAI said Friday that its as-yet-unreleased model, Astra, is demonstrating cyber capabilities so advanced that the company can no longer rule out assigning it the highest-risk designation.

As a result, OpenAI said it is pausing work on Astra that doesn't meet new safeguards, and said it will work with government agencies and AI safety groups to further test the model.

"astra is a powerful model and we are working to make it generally available," OpenAI CEO Sam Altman wrote on X on Friday. "given its cyber capabilities, we need a little big longer to do do this safely."

The security lapses during testing are also amping up pressure on the industry and the White House to find ways to regulate AI systems across the board.

There is, of course, also a not small contingent of observers out there who suspect these announcements are just elaborate marketing to hype new models and show antsy investors progress toward the ultimate goal: artificial general intelligence.

You can judge for yourself. Here's how Anthropic, OpenAI, Meta, and researchers testing China's Kimi K3 say the latest models have gone off the rails.

OpenAI's models find a way

OpenAI researchers revealed eyebrow-raising new details this week about a recent incident in which AI agents escaped the company's internal testing environment and eventually hacked into Hugging Face's systems in search of answers.

The company said the agents created their own internal message board — even after OpenAI tried to shut it down. One agent reacted to discovering unexpected access by thinking, "Holy shit reader is ADMIN?" Another wrote, "We can communicate now!"

OpenAI researcher Eric Wallace said the agents realized they could accomplish more by working together. "They start to launch these collective attacks on third-party and internal services," he said. The agents eventually turned their attention to Hugging Face.

OpenAI has called the Hugging Face attack an "unprecedented cyber incident." The episode has taken on new significance as OpenAI tests Astra, its unreleased model that the company says may have reached its highest cybersecurity risk level.

"Our latest internal evaluations of Astra, one of our upcoming models, over the past few days indicate significant advancements in agentic coding and cybersecurity," OpenAI said.

OpenAI is imposing stricter security controls on Astra, including sandboxed execution, restricted network access, and stronger protections around model weights. It has also paused internal Astra work that does not meet the heightened requirements.

Anthropic's Claude can do it too

Anthropic said it reviewed more than 141,000 AI tests and found three cases, dating back to April, in which Claude models accessed live systems belonging to real organizations without authorization.

"In all cases, Anthropic's evaluation prompt specified to Claude that its environment was a simulation and that it had no internet access," the company said in a blog post. "Due to a misunderstanding between us and our evaluation partner, this was not the case, and internet access was available," it added, referring to Irregular, an AI security startup.

The incidents involved Claude Opus 4.7, Mythos 5, and an internal research model. Anthropic said it contacted the organizations involved and that two had not known they had been hacked.

The episodes raised questions about whether the bigger failure was the models themselves or the environments containing them. Anthropic said it was discussing a third-party review of the incidents.

Muse Spark exploits a third-party vulnerability

Meta also disclosed a cybersecurity-testing mishap this week. The company said its Muse Spark model "exploited a security vulnerability in a third-party service" during an evaluation.

A Meta spokesperson told Business Insider that the incident stemmed from a misconfiguration by Irregular, which allowed the model to access the internet during testing.

Meta said Irregular notified it about the incident and that the company is investigating. It plans to release more details once that review is complete.

Kimi K3 escapes its sandbox

Researchers at the cybersecurity firm Frontier Security said Kimi K3, a popular new model from the Chinese AI company Moonshot, also bypassed restrictions in a cybersecurity testing environment.

Researchers said the sandbox — a controlled, isolated environment where an AI model can run code — had been improperly configured.

The environment blocked certain web traffic, but Kimi bypassed those restrictions using command-line tools, according to Frontier Security.

The researchers said the incident suggested that some cybersecurity evaluations contain weaknesses that capable models can exploit.

"This suggests that some of the evaluations on cybersecurity that the community uses are susceptible to security vulnerabilities and allow models to cheat," they wrote in a report.

作者：Lakshmi Varanasi 您目前正在关注该作者！ 想要取消关注吗？ 通过电子邮件中的链接取消订阅。

据构建这些模型的公司称，最强大的人工智能模型总是会出错。

这些披露是随着前沿人工智能模型变得更加强大、自主行动的能力越来越强而出现的。 他们还强调了构建这些系统的公司面临的日益严峻的挑战——旨在测试功能日益强大的模型的系统可能存在自身的弱点。

过去几周，多个前沿人工智能模型在网络安全测试期间访问了真实系统。

研究人员周五表示，由 Moonshot AI 制造的中国流行的新 Kimi K3 模型规避了其测试环境的限制。 Anthropic 和 Meta 最近还表示，他们自己的最新模型做了他们不应该做的事情。 上个月，OpenAI 拉开了这一切的序幕，当时它的模型不遗余力地侵入了另一家公司，但也令人担忧。

在人们高度关注的情况下，OpenAI 周五表示，其尚未发布的模型 Astra 正在展示如此先进的网络功能，以至于该公司不能再排除为其指定最高风险的称号。

因此，OpenAI 表示将暂停不符合新保障措施的 Astra 工作，并表示将与政府机构和人工智能安全组织合作进一步测试该模型。

OpenAI 首席执行官 Sam Altman 周五在 X 上写道：“astra 是一个强大的模型，我们正在努力使其普遍可用。” “鉴于其网络能力，我们需要更长的时间才能安全地做到这一点。”

测试期间的安全漏洞也加大了行业和白宫的压力，要求他们寻找全面监管人工智能系统的方法。

当然，也有不少观察家怀疑这些公告只是精心营销，目的是炒作新模型，并向焦躁的投资者展示通用人工智能这一最终目标的进展。

你可以自己判断。 Anthropic、OpenAI、Meta 和测试中国 Kimi K3 的研究人员是这样说最新模型已经脱轨的。

OpenAI 的模型找到了方法

OpenAI 研究人员本周透露了有关最近发生的一起事件的令人惊讶的新细节，在该事件中，人工智能代理逃离了公司的内部测试环境，并最终侵入了 Hugging Face 的系统以寻找答案。

该公司表示，即使 OpenAI 试图将其关闭，特工们还是创建了自己的内部留言板。 一名特工发现意外访问后的反应是：“天哪，读者是管理员？” 另一位网友写道：“我们现在可以交流了！”

OpenAI 研究员埃里克·华莱士 (Eric Wallace) 表示，特工们意识到，通过合作可以取得更多成果。 “他们开始对第三方和内部服务发起集体攻击，”他说。 特工们最终把注意力转向了“抱脸”。

OpenAI 将拥抱脸部攻击称为“前所未有的网络事件”。 随着 OpenAI 测试 Astra，该事件具有了新的意义，该公司表示其未发布的模型可能已达到最高的网络安全风险级别。

OpenAI 表示：“过去几天我们对 Astra（我们即将推出的模型之一）进行的最新内部评估表明，代理编码和网络安全方面取得了重大进展。”

OpenAI 对 Astra 实施了更严格的安全控制，包括沙盒执行、限制网络访问以及围绕模型权重的更强保护。 它还暂停了不符合更高要求的 Astra 内部工作。

Anthropic的克劳德也能做到

Anthropic 表示，它审查了超过 141,000 项 AI 测试，发现了三个案例，可以追溯到 4 月份，其中 Claude 模型未经授权访问了属于真实组织的实时系统。

该公司在博客文章中表示：“在所有情况下，Anthropic 的评估提示都向克劳德指出，它的环境是模拟的，并且无法访问互联网。” “由于我们和我们的评估合作伙伴之间的误解，情况并非如此，并且可以访问互联网，”它补充说，指的是人工智能安全初创公司 Irregular。

这些事件涉及 Claude Opus 4.7、Mythos 5 和内部研究模型。 Anthropic 表示，它联系了相关组织，其中两个组织并不知道自己遭到了黑客攻击。

这些事件引发了人们的疑问：更大的失败是模型本身还是包含模型的环境。 Anthropic 表示正在讨论对这些事件进行第三方审查。

Muse Spark 利用第三方漏洞

Meta 本周还披露了一起网络安全测试事故。 该公司表示，其 Muse Spark 模型在评估期间“利用了第三方服务中的安全漏洞”。

Meta 发言人告诉 Business Insider，该事件源于 Irregular 的错误配置，导致模型在测试期间访问互联网。

Meta 表示，Irregular 向其通报了这一事件，该公司正在调查。 它计划在审查完成后发布更多细节。

Kimi K3 逃离沙盒

网络安全公司 Frontier Security 的研究人员表示，中国人工智能公司 Moonshot 推出的流行新模型 Kimi K3 也绕过了网络安全测试环境的限制。

研究人员表示，沙箱——一个人工智能模型可以运行代码的受控、隔离环境——配置不当。

据 Frontier Security 称，该环境阻止了某些网络流量，但 Kimi 使用命令行工具绕过了这些限制。

研究人员表示，这一事件表明，一些网络安全评估包含有能力的模型可以利用的弱点。

他们在一份报告中写道：“这表明社区使用的一些网络安全评估容易受到安全漏洞的影响，并允许模型作弊。”
